text:
alex: quick proposal — trying to shrink the gap between postmortem writeups and actual remediations. idea: a lightweight remediation sprintboard + a simple comms cadence + small IC rotation tweak. putting a draft here for feedback.

maria: love this. can you outline what the sprintboard columns look like?

alex: sure. thinking minimal: Backlog / In Progress / Needs Review / Verified / Closed. owners + a designated secondary on every card. weekly triage to move items into the sprint.

devon: +1. also add a 'recurrence-watch' tag for items tied to repeating alerts so we can prioritize.

alex: yep — recurrence tag is key. also propose SLA tiers on closure: P0/P1 must have mitigation or rollback within 7d, full remediation within 30d; P2 within 60d; lower risk 90d. these are just starting numbers.

alex: quick timeline template we can copy into each postmortem:```
Owner: <name>
Secondary: <name>
Priority: P0/P1/P2
Created: <iso-ts>
Target mitigation date (soft): <30d / 60d / 90d>
Target verification: <owner-verifies + oncall signoff>
Acceptance criteria: <what counts as done>
Notes: <monitoring/alerts to add>
Tags: recurrence, root-cause-category
```

susan: that template is nice and small. can we automate reminders and status updates?

oncall-bot: reminder automation idea: when a postmortem action is created, create card + set due date, then send reminders at 7d/14d/3d before due. ping owner in-thread and #eng-oncall weekly digest.

tim: question on cadence — how long is the weekly triage? who runs it?

alex: propose 30-minute triage every Monday 10am. rotating chair = incident-commander of that week (we already rotate ICs). chair responsibilities: move highest-risk items into sprint, confirm owners, escalate blockers.

maria: rotating chair is fine. can we have a small quarterly review of recurring incidents and pattern analysis? we keep fixing symptoms but not the systemic stuff.

devon: +1. proposed quarterly agenda: top recurring alerts, actions taken, blockers preventing full remediation, infra changes needed. include Product if customer impact is recurring.

alex: operational notes:
- require 'secondary' on every action (so ownership survives PTO).
- require acceptance criteria on creation (prevents vague 'do some cleanup').
- close only after oncall verifies in-prod behaviour for 48h (or agreed verification window).

susan: how do we surface regressions? add a dashboard that links cards -> alert timelines?

devon: attach the alert id(s) and a small 'recurrence score' computed from last 90 days. helps sorting.

alex: implementation plan (MVP):
1) create a simple board in our existing tracker (labels + columns) — week 0.
2) add template + require fields when creating action.
3) hook oncall-bot to post weekly digest and due reminders.
4) run 3 weekly sprints, measure closure rate and time-to-close, adjust SLAs.

tim: metrics we should track: median time-to-closure, % actions with secondary assigned, % actions with acceptance criteria, recurrence rate for top 10 alerts.

maria: timeline? can we pilot for 6 weeks then present to eng leadership?

alex: pilot next Monday -> 6 weeks -> review. I'll spin up the board and the template today and ping folks.

oncall-bot: created: https://tracker.internal/board/PM-sprintboard (demo link) — owners please add actions from recent postmortems.

devon: adding items now. tagging items with recurrence scores.

susan: thanks alex — can you also put a short how-to (1 pager) in docs so new ICs know their chair duties for triage?

alex: will do. rough checklist will be in the board description + short doc in /docs/incident-followup.md.

tim: tiny detail: rotate IC chairs only among oncall rotation list, not product or execs. keeps it operational.

alex: agreed. final ask: everyone who owns open postmortem actions this week, please add secondary and acceptance criteria before EOD Friday. I'll follow up in a thread. :thumbsup:
